stories.title: Trump revisits Malvinas War in UK interview: ‘It’s a long time ago’
stories.summary: United States President Donald Trump chose not to answer if the U.S. would support the United Kingdom in a potential new conflict with Argentina over the Malvinas Islands. In an interview with British outlet GB News on Thursday, he chose instead to praise the British military for regaining the islands in the 1982 war, while also saying that the war was a “long time ago.” “Well look, I was there when they had the first war. That was a long time ago, and I watched it so carefully, and you comported yourselves very well. You took it back pretty strongly, but it’s a long way away. That’s a big trip; it’s a long way,” Trump said. The Republican’s response was presented as “a threat” by the British outlet on its website and caused reactions from the media and political figures. While the Daily Mail said that Trump “hinted” that he wouldn’t back Britain if Argentina invaded the islands, Labour MP Anna Turley responded to the U.S. President’s statements by reaffirming her government’s position. “The Falklands are British and will remain British,” she stated. Trump’s suggestive remarks came just hours before President Javier Milei is due to deliver a nationally televised address, reportedly to announce measures concerning the disputed area. In early August, the libertarian president claimed that the United States had an interest in Argentina holding sovereignty over the islands in order to guarantee security in the South Atlantic. Milei highlighted the strategic relationship with Washington at the time and said that ties with the United States “will be key to recovering” Argentina’s sovereignty over the islands.
